mechanism: rev0 anchor = bytes FF 1F (call far [bx]) at arena in-page 52h/53h, written by A 0066-006B (mov ax,1FFFh; stosw; dec di; call far [bx]) at DI=xxA2 in ES=FAR_SEG 0FFBh (A 0029 'B0 A2', A 004A '81 CA FB 0F'; B 0031/0077 'B0 A2', B 0096). The MOVSW twin (counter in scratch/B060/movsw53_A/B.asm = B051 cMovsw: only 'B0 A2' -> 'B0 A3' in A and B) pushes 'A5 hh FB 0F' with A5 at addresses = 3 mod 4. When its trail crosses our anchor it writes A5 at 53h -> FF A5 d16 = jmp [di+d16] (memory exception, B051 trace pkj3o), and the next push writes 0F at 52h. The anchor residue (=2 mod 4) is fixed by AL=A2 (the pushed IP low byte A4 must land on the anchor as the rebuild trigger), so no lattice or FAR_SEG choice in the MOVSB design avoids it. Each extra twin adds another lethal trail over our anchor: losses compound (rev0 keeps 82% / 59% / 25% of the control score with 1/2/3 twins), while the twins themselves rise above fair share (0.31-0.38).

recommendation: No promotion candidate. The only multi-copy threat that compounds is a crowd of strong MOVSW-family replicators (a V6 twin with AL=A3h): 3 copies leave rev0 at 0.06/battle. It is structural (anchor residue fixed by the A4 rebuild trigger) and has no cheap fix: lattice shift helps partially (+0.08) but loses -0.12 vs a cgx crowd and -0.01 on the screen. Prevalence in the 2025/2024 pools is nil (real MOVSW codes are weak), so treat it as a 2026 risk only if published V6-like code gets a MOVSW variant. Undercut clones and mixed counter fields do not compound.
